coaching.headline: More kills, fewer towers: a winnable game lost at an uncontested Primal Fangtooth.
coaching.team: Four of five lanes read unfavored in the draft; only the jungle read favored early, where Aurora held an edge over Khaimera. Kwang opened the game with first blood on Sevarog at 5.5 minutes, and three of Kwang's five kills all game came on that same lane. The team still built a real lead: three Fangtooths by 23 minutes, both seedlings, and 21 river buffs to the opponents' 15. That lead evaporated at 31 minutes, when the opponents secured their Primal Fangtooth completely uncontested, with every one of the five alive. Genesis Core and an Orb Prime both fell their way within the next three minutes, and the deficit never closed. The offlane sat out eight of the eleven logged fights, pinned in a lane never won back. That included the two costliest losses of the night: the fight at their outer tower (21.2), lost 0-3, and the fight at our inhibitor (38.1), lost 1-4. Those two fed a tower and both inhibitors within about a minute each time. The game finished 29-19 on kills and 7-9 on towers. Next game: get the offlane into fights before the tower or inhibitor is already gone, not after.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: What actually flipped this game? At 31 minutes, the opponents' Primal Fangtooth secure went completely uncontested, and nobody on our side was even dead beforehand — this isn't a numbers problem, it's a map-presence one. Genesis Core and an Orb Prime both fell their way in the next three minutes off the back of that stack, and the gap never closed.
coaching.whatWorked: The one clean pattern that held up: won fights actually turned into progress more often than the opponents managed. The squad won six fights and cashed four of them into an objective or tower within the window, against four wins and two cashes for the opponents — real conversion, even if it wasn't enough to close the towers gap.

perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Phase's lane read theirs all game against Riktor, and the flagged absences show why: pinned there, Mr_Meat31 sat out eight of the eleven logged fights. In the three fights reached, Mr_Meat31 died in every one — the loss at their outer tower (21.2), the win at the inner tower (24.7), and the loss at the inhibitor (38.1). Fifteen assists and 27,449 healing show the support work was there when the fight could be reached.

From 15 minutes on, Sevarog was flagged absent from eight of the eleven logged fights, including the two costliest losses of the night, at 21.2 and 38.1. Only three deaths all game, tied for the fewest on the team, and a team-high 78,140 damage mitigated. The lane never got contested back, and the team's only listed frontline hero missed most of the fights that decided the game.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Skylar's lane read unfavored against Drongo on paper, and the result said otherwise: eighteen kills against five deaths, with 73,441 damage to heroes, the highest of any player in the lobby. Skylar won the skirmish at our Fangtooth alone, 3-0, and later closed another near our inner tower, 2-0, both largely solo work. The build skipped Imperator, the meta core's third piece, for Terminus, Tainted Rounds, and Sky Splitter instead, trading crit damage for lifesteal and the team's only marksman-side anti-heal.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Aurora's jungle matchup read ours early, even late against Khaimera, and the early edge was real. But nine deaths, the most on either side, turned this into the costliest role on the team: five of them fed directly into an enemy objective or tower afterward, including the double-inhibitor loss at 38.5 and the Orb Prime and Core sequence that ended the game at 40.4. Three of those nine deaths were solo catches, caught alone between 29.3 and 34 minutes with no fight nearby.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.text: Absent from eight of eleven logged fights, pinned in a support lane that read theirs all game against Riktor. Died in all three fights reached — the losses at 21.2 and 38.1, and the win at 24.7. Fifteen assists and 27,449 healing when the fight could be reached.

acc1906e-6177-41a3-9c5c-f151757fee86.text: Lost the first half of mid to Gideon, four of six deaths, then flipped it, killing Gideon three times in the second half. The full six-item build was pure magical power with nothing spent on survivability.

a1a53d3e-2074-4410-9d59-cc7fce1e63e2.text: Lost the lane to Kwang all game — three of Kwang's five kills came on Sevarog, including the first blood at 5.5. From 15 minutes on, flagged absent from eight of eleven fights, including both of the night's costliest losses. Only three deaths all game, tied for the fewest on the team. The lane never got contested back.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.text: Eighteen kills to five deaths, 73,441 damage to heroes, the highest of any player in the lobby. Won two fights essentially alone: the fight at our Fangtooth (22.9), won 3-0, and the fight at our inner tower (25.7), won 2-0. The build skipped Imperator for lifesteal and anti-heal instead, and it worked.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.text: Nine deaths, the most on either side. Drongo alone got five of them, and five of the nine directly preceded an enemy objective or tower falling. The early jungle edge over Khaimera never carried into the rest of the game.

40.4.call: This fight was won 5-2 at their Orb Prime, but Aurora's death in it, at 40.4, came about a minute before that Prime secured and the Core fell at 41.2, with The Fey dead by then too. The call there was to prioritize denying or contesting the Prime once the fight turned, since losing both left nobody there to stop it — that objective decided the game more than the extra kills did.

38.1.call: The team held at our inhibitor with Sevarog still pinned in a losing offlane lane, absent from the fight, and lost it 1-4 anyway. That cost both inhibitors within about a minute, at 39.5 and 39.7. Skipping that fight until the offlane could join would likely have cost less than two inhibitors.

21.2.call: Losing 0-3 at their outer tower fed a tower loss of our own about a minute later, at 22.4. The Fey was alive and never joined that fight, and Sevarog was pinned in a losing lane the same way — fighting away from home without two of five up is a call to skip, and defending back instead likely keeps that tower standing.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Mr_Meat31 covered Phase's full meta core (Marshal, Enra's Blessing, Galaxy Greaves), including Enra's Blessing's shield for an immobilized ally within range — real value against Riktor's pull-into-silence-into-suppress chain. The last three slots went to Prophecy, Plasma Blade, and Spectra, three on-hit or ability-power items built for more damage rather than survivability. Against a comp built around a chainable hard-crowd-control combo, the alternative path, a defensive item with built-in tenacity like Unbroken Will, would have helped Phase survive the suppress instead of adding damage from a hero who finished with zero kills. The trade mattered most given Phase died in all three fights reached this game.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: The engine's top-modeled major for Phase support is Vesh, an ability-damage blessing that adds a damage tick to her spells — it lines up with a passive that already heals off ability casts, letting Phase chip health while sustaining herself and a linked ally. The default minors add haste on takedowns and bonus damage against high-health targets, leaning the loadout toward extended teamfights rather than one burst window. The trade-off is that Vesh spends its budget on damage rather than survivability, so a Phase running it still needs the item slots to cover the survivability a chain-crowd-control comp like this one demands.

acc1906e-6177-41a3-9c5c-f151757fee86.build: The Fey's six items were all magical power, ability haste, and penetration, with zero health or armor across the whole build: Combustion, Caustica, Oblivion Crown, Noxia, Astral Catalyst, and Megacosm. The Fey skipped Wraith Leggings, the meta core's third piece (extra magic penetration and movement speed), for Caustica and Noxia instead, both similar burst-damage mage items, plus Astral Catalyst, which cuts the value of enemy shields — a reasonable tech pick against Riktor's shield-on-CC passive. The real gap: a hero whose win condition is landing a teamfight pull needs to survive long enough to cast it. Four of six deaths came from the same hero, Gideon, including being caught alone at 11.8.
acc1906e-6177-41a3-9c5c-f151757fee86.eternal: The engine's top-modeled major for The Fey in midlane is Demiurge, which scales stats and item-effect damage off however many items are completed — a natural fit for a mage who wants a full six-item power spike online before committing to fights. The trade is the same one the items already made: Demiurge is weak early and offers nothing defensive, so a lane that goes theirs early, the way this one read against Gideon, gets punished before the blessing pays out.

a1a53d3e-2074-4410-9d59-cc7fce1e63e2.build: Sevarog covered two of the meta core's three pieces, Tainted Guard and Fist Of Razuul, but skipped Fire Blossom, an armor-and-health item, for Cybernetic Drive, Flux Matrix, Inquisition, and Raiment of Renewal instead, all tank-class defensive items in their own right, just not the specific one the field runs most. Tainted Guard brought anti-heal, cutting healing on whoever lands a hit, which mattered against a Khaimera and Riktor both leaning on sustain. Sevarog died three times, all to Kwang, including the first blood at 5.5, and that lane matchup never got contested back.
a1a53d3e-2074-4410-9d59-cc7fce1e63e2.eternal: The engine's top-modeled major for Sevarog offlane is Krix, a flat health-stacking blessing that fits a hero whose own passive already stacks permanent health and damage off ability kills — more raw health compounds directly with Souls. The default minors add a healing cut on damage-over-time effects and permanent health on takedowns, both suited to grinding out the long fight this kit wants. The trade is early-game power: Krix pays out in bulk over time, which lines up poorly with a lane already lost to Kwang by 9 minutes in this game.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Skylar covered two of the meta core's three pieces, Plasma Blade and Vanquisher (which brings an execute below 5% health), but skipped Imperator, the crit-damage amplifier, for Terminus, Tainted Rounds, and Sky Splitter instead. Those three lean into lifesteal and armor shred rather than raw crit damage, and Tainted Rounds gave the team its only marksman-side anti-heal against Khaimera's sustain and Riktor's healing. It was a fair trade for a night that ran on solo picks: eighteen kills, most of them one-for-one, rather than one big grouped burst that Imperator would have amplified.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: The engine's top-modeled major for Skylar carry is Demiurge, which scales off completed items and rewards exactly the six-item build reached this game. The trade is the same one the items already made: nothing early and nothing defensive, so the loadout's value depends on staying alive long enough to get there.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Aurora covered the full meta core (Magnify, Elafrost, Gaia Greaves, the last two carrying physical armor) and added Tainted Scepter for anti-heal against Khaimera's sustain, plus Flux Matrix for more magic armor — a defensively minded build on paper. A sixth item never got finished; nine deaths, the most on either side, kept resetting the gold clock. Three of those deaths were solo catches with no fight nearby, between 29.3 and 34 minutes, and that pattern mattered more than the item choices did.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: The engine's top-modeled major for Aurora in jungle is Demiurge, an item-scaling blessing that rewards a completed build — the six-item power spike this game's build never reached. The trade-off is real: Demiurge offers nothing early and nothing defensive, a genuine gamble for a jungler who gets caught alone, which is exactly what happened three times this game.

threats: Chain-CC risk (4 hard-CC abilities, ~3.0s of lockdown): Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s), Kwang Surge of the Heavens (knockup 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Riktor. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Our damage is 4/5 magical — predictable; one magic-resist item answers most of it. Mix in a physical threat.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.passive: abilities heal her and her linked ally

ourKits.playAgainst: kill the linked carry, not Phase; break the link timing
